clue.text: Impromptu score

definitions.meaning: a ... team or meal is thrown together on the spot
to score a surface is to mark it with a line or scrape

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit one word: an improvised, makeshift thing, and a mark or scrape on a surface.

clue.text: Friendly party

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means sociable or companionable; as a noun it names an informal gathering of club members.

clue.text: Fashion earclip is a repro wheel?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Fashion earclip is a repro wheel? (7)': EARCLIP anagrams to the answer with 'a repro' as definition, but 'wheel?' has no job; the OCR text looks corrupted and no source was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Fashion earclip is a repro wheel?

clue.text: Highwayman's character changed finally, due, perhaps, to depravity

indicators.note: the last letter of the highwayman's name is swapped for a different one

parts.note: Dick Turpin was the most famous English highwayman of the eighteenth century

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of due appear in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A highwayman's nature finally altered, owing perhaps to his wicked ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character changed finally' replaces Turpin's last letter N with T, giving TURPIT; 'perhaps' turns DUE into UDE. Dick Turpin was a notorious English highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is wickedness or moral baseness, a close synonym of depravity.

clue.text: Lay up and isolate hips for replacement

indicators.note: hip replacement suggests surgery, but here it says the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A patient is admitted and kept apart while awaiting new hip joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for replacement' rearranges ISOLATE plus HIPS, eleven letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: To be laid up is to be confined to bed through illness, which a hospital admission does.

clue.text: Jessie's exploits out of print

definitions.note: read as 'Jessie is': the definition plus a link

parts.note: to milk someone is to exploit them

explanation.surface: Jessie takes advantage of things no longer published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jessie' is British slang for a weak, effeminate man, so 'Jessie's' reads as 'a Jessie is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, timid man, which is what the British slang jessie means.

clue.text: Fifth of November and no old penny for the guy!

indicators.note: picks the fifth letter of the word that follows
no says a letter is dropped from the word and

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for the pre-decimal British penny

explanation.surface: Bonfire Night, and a guy made without spending a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Fifth of November (Bonfire Night) suggests the Guy Fawkes effigy, but it is just letter five of NOVEMBER. Pre-1971 British pennies were abbreviated d.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is an informal word for a male person, a fellow.

clue.text: The wine of France laid cannibal down like lightning, once

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The wine of France laid cannibal down like lightning, once (5)': LE VIN plus definition 'lightning, once' works, but 'laid cannibal down like' has no job; OCR text appears corrupted and no source was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: The wine of France laid cannibal down like lightning, once

clue.text: Bronze troublesome to hide?

parts.note: a tan that hurts, where the hide is a person's skin rather than something concealed

explanation.surface: A bronze statue proves hard to conceal.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide is skin, and bronze is a tan colour, so a painful tan on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Overexposure to sunshine reddens and blisters the skin, a painful kind of tan.

clue.text: One provides economy flight, beating rush

parts.note: a pulse is a beating, as of the heart
a jet is a rush or spurt of liquid or gas

explanation.surface: A budget airline whose flights are always a mad dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse-jet is a simple, cheap jet engine that fires in intermittent bursts.

clue.text: Accountant, with capital, advanced something to put on a horse

definitions.text: something to put on a horse

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
Paris is the capital of France
on means forward, advanced

explanation.surface: An accountant puts capital forward for some piece of horse equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth or covering laid over a horse's saddle and harness.

clue.text: Civic Centre on Back Lane is for sale

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word Civic is taken
Back says the word Lane is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: The civic centre on Back Lane is on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' takes V from CIVIC; 'Back' turns LANE into ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A venal official can be bought, so is corruptly purchasable.

clue.text: One on bail freed with this excuse

indicators.note: freed says the letters of bail are released into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A prisoner released on bail uses this as an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, the classic excuse against a criminal charge.

clue.text: Sealed agreement, wearing false smile

parts.note: in clothes means wearing them
a denture gives a smile of false teeth

explanation.surface: A contract signed with an insincere grin.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal sealed contract, notably binding an apprentice.

clue.text: Indisposed, small dose is given maenad given

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Indisposed, small dose is given maenad given (11)': D + IS + INCLINED is plausible, but 'maenad given' is garbled OCR and no source was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Indisposed, small dose is given maenad given

clue.text: One considered certain to succeed — having skill in physics, say

parts.note: a natural is someone born to do something, sure to succeed
science in its older sense means skill or expertise

explanation.surface: A born winner who is also adept at physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Physics is one example of the disciplines studying the physical world, alongside chemistry and biology.

clue.text: Travelling, one can take time with good books

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a tin is a can
an era is a period of time
NT is the New Testament, part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: A traveller who can find time for the scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant worker moves from place to place, so is always on the road.

clue.text: Elite wearing diamonds in nail the coldest part of Alaska?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Elite wearing diamonds in nail the coldest part of Alaska? (3-5)': CREAM in ICE fits, but 'in nail' has no job (perhaps 'is' misread beyond the allowed changes); no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Elite wearing diamonds in nail the coldest part of Alaska?

clue.text: Bottle-imp gets a resident vicar drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person's words are jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A tipsy local clergyman ends up with a genie in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges A RESIDENT VICAR, fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle-imp is the old name for the toy where a small figure in a water-filled bottle rises and sinks when squeezed.

clue.text: Rugby revival, so bucolic? france

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Rugby revival, so bucolic? france (7)': RU + RALLY fits, but the trailing 'france' is garbled OCR with no job; no source found.

clue.text: Nearest translation is oriental

indicators.note: a translation renders words in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The nearest rendering of a text is an Asian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things of Asia or the East.

clue.text: Bloke reported in the Inner Wheel?

indicators.note: reported says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a fellow is a bloke, a man

explanation.surface: A man mentioned in the records of a women's service club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inner Wheel is a women's club linked to Rotary, but here it is the wheel's inner rim, which the spokes join beneath the tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A felloe is the rim of a wooden wheel, to which the spokes attach inside the tyre.

clue.text: Athlete's turn to impress the field?

definitions.meaning: the rim of a ... presses a track into a field

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a sideways gymnastic flip; the other is the wheel of a farm cart leaving its mark.

clue.text: Off-white willow binding

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pale-coloured willow tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-white' looks like a colour, but 'Off' rearranges WHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A withe is a pliable willow twig used for tying or binding.

clue.text: What's to follow a portion of canteen suet?

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking what comes after a helping of canteen suet pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards, to follow as a result.

clue.text: City area almost delayed this conspicuous success

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is cut off the word for delayed

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: Arriving late in the City still brings great success.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London's postal district.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliant success or striking acclaim.

clue.text: Peach of an apple

definitions.meaning: a peach is an excellent person or thing, one without equal
An old variety of dessert apple

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an unrivalled example of something, and a traditional variety of eating apple.

clue.text: Almost done-up? Sleep!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read bottom to top
almost says the last letter is cut off the word

explanation.surface: Nearly ready? Time to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts DONE to DON; 'up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to doze briefly, the head dropping in light sleep.

clue.text: Puny person after hawthorn or dog-fennel

indicators.note: after puts the weakling's word behind the blossom's

parts.note: may is another name for hawthorn blossom
a weed is a weak, skinny person

explanation.surface: A weakling chasing a hawthorn bush or a smelly plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayweed is a wild chamomile also called dog-fennel, a strong-smelling plant.

clue.text: Helping poor relations from France

parts.note: suggests charity to needy kin, but means easing strained international ties, with a French term

explanation.surface: Aiding hard-up relatives from across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Poor relations here are bad diplomatic ties, not needy family.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is a French word for the relaxing of tension between rival states.
